summary: Edgar Howard Sturtevant (1875–1952) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Illinois College and Indiana University Bloomington, later holding academic posts at Columbia University (circa 1907–1920) and Yale University (circa 1923–1943).

Edgar Polomé (1920–2000) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. After studying at the Catholic University of Louvain from around 1940 to 1949, he served at the University of Texas at Austin from circa 1961 to 2000, becoming professor emeritus.

Edith Wyschogrod (1930–2009) worked in philosophy and religious studies. She earned degrees from Hunter College and Columbia University, and served as the J. Newton Rayzor Professor of Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University from 1992 to 2002.

Edmond Yee (b. 1938) is a scholar in religious studies and sinology. He served on the faculties of both Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union from circa 1986 to 2006.

Edmund Hardy (1852–1904) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Mainz, Berlin, Heidelberg (PhD under Kuno Fischer), and Freiburg, later serving as professor of philosophy at Freiburg (1885–1893) and chair at Fribourg (1894–1898).

Edmund Leach (1910–1989) worked in religious studies and related fields. Educated at Cambridge and the LSE, he held posts as lecturer at the LSE, professor at Cambridge (1953–1978), provost of King's College, Cambridge (1966–1979), and RAI president (1971–1975).
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder (1863–1896) was an Indologist. He graduated from Harvard University in 1886 and studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Edo Shonin works in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Eduard Böhmer (1827–1906) was a linguist who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1847–1851). He later held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1859–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (circa 1872–1879).

Eduard Erkes (1891–1958) was a sinologist who studied at Leipzig University under August Conrady, whom he later succeeded. He held posts at Leipzig University (circa 1917–1958) and the Humboldt University of Berlin.

Eduard Hermann (1869–1950) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Leipzig, Freiburg, and Jena under Berthold Delbrück, and held posts at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and Göttingen (1917–1937), succeeding Jacob Wackernagel.

Eduard Müller-Hess (1853–1923) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed an Inauguraldissertation at Leipzig University in 1874 and was attested as a professor at the University of Bern in 1897–1898.

Eduard Röer (1805–1866) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Königsberg and Jena under Herbart and Bopp, held a postdoctorate at Berlin (1833), and served at the East India Company and the Asiatic Society.

Eduard Sachau (1845–1930) was an Orientalist and linguist. Educated at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle under Brockhaus, Fleischer, and Nöldeke, he held professorships at the University of Vienna and the University of Berlin, and directed the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen.

Eduard Schwyzer (1874–1943) worked in linguistics and Indology. He succeeded Adolf Kaegi in 1914 and held academic posts at the University of Zurich (circa 1912–1927), University of Bonn (circa 1927–1932), and Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1932–1943).

Eduard Sievers (1850–1932) was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Curtius and Leskien. He held professorships at Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and Leipzig (1892–1922).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

Edvard Westermarck (1862–1939) was a philosopher and scholar who studied at the University of Helsinki (circa 1881–1889). He held academic posts at the London School of Economics (circa 1904–1930) and Åbo Akademi University (circa 1918–1932).

Edward Albert Gait (1863–1950) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at University College London, founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914, and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick (1814–1883) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Charterhouse, Merton College, and Oxford. He served as Professor of Hindustani and Telugu at East India Company College (1845) and held a post at the Foreign Office.
